messages:
alana: Heads-up: after the 2026-03-17 rollout (merge 1f3a2b9) we've seen a Dedicated pool start spiking OOMs for longctx requests (seqlen > 2k). Alerting shows memory climbing steadily until OOM. Not a CPU spike, just memory growth.

miguel: saw the alerts. are these new hosts or existing capacity? any correlation with kernel-selection or batching changes in that merge? :thinking:

alana: existing Dedicated cluster. The merge included a batching heuristic tweak + a kernel-selection fallback for quantized kernels. I ran a quick pmap on a crashed pid and saw a lot of small anonymous mappings and repeated allocations around 1-8kb.

perf-bot: CI perf regression detected: memory P50 +3.6% on inference-longctx suite, throughput steady. Link: https://ci.internal/rounds/5423 (run 5423)

dmitri: Can someone run a heap snapshot/gcore when it reproduces? Also please attach jemalloc stats: `MALLOC_CONF=stats_print:true` or use the allocator hook.

alana: attached quick snippets from the node that OOMed: \n```\n[OOM] signal 6, pid=13245\njemalloc stats: active: 11.3G, retained: 2.4G, allocated: 9.8G\nhot slab buckets: lots of 8kb entries, back-to-back allocations from kv cache warmup path\nbacktrace (sample): runtime::alloc_kv_entry -> kv_warmup_prefetch -> kernel_router::handoff\n```\n
miguel: Interesting. The kernel-selection change moved some requests to the new fast-quant path which increases per-entry metadata (adds 64B header + align to 8k pagelets). On typical short-ctx this is negligible, but with longctx and our slab sizing it fragments badly.

sarah: I started a bisect on the release branch to confirm: `git bisect start --first-parent v2026.03` -> found regression introduced by `1f3a2b9` (batching heur + kernel fallback). dmitri, can you sanity-check the commit?

dmitri: Confirmed. Reproduced locally with `perf sim` + long prompts (len ~3500). Reproducer: `./inference_test --model=redwood-medium --seqlen=3500 --clients=8 --warmup=2` -> memory steadily climbs. Bisect points at the kernel-selection switch where we added `prefer_fast_quant_if_compatible`.

alana: Proposed mitigations: 1) rollback the kernel fallback in a canary, 2) temporarily disable kv warmup prefetch on Dedicated (soft-prefetch off), or 3) tune slab bucket sizes / reduce reserve for shard-reserve. Which path is fastest for rollout?

miguel: Fastest is toggle soft-prefetch off via rollout flag, we can flip it cluster-wide in ~10m and observe. Revert the merge takes longer (infra approvals). Let's flip the flag and hold the rollout for the release.

dmitri: Agreed. Also captured perf flame samples showing hot path in `kv_fill_small_entry` with many cache misses. Suggest we add a guard: if seqlen > 2048 avoid fast-quant kernel to prevent bigger metadata allocation. That would be a targeted fix.

sarah: I'll open a hotfix PR to (a) disable soft-prefetch by default for Dedicated, (b) add seqlen guard in kernel router, and (c) add a CI test that exercises seqlen 4k to catch regressions. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4821

perf-bot: Performance test queued for PR 4821. Baseline vs candidate diff will post results when done.

alana: After flipping soft-prefetch off on the canary pool memory stabilized. No further OOMs in the last 20m. Marking rollout hold.

miguel: Nice. Next steps: get dmitri's seqlen-guard in, add allocator telemetry (per-slab occupancy over time), and plan a postmortem on why kernel-selection increased per-entry metadata without a perf ownership review.

dmitri: I'll include a small microbenchmark that measures per-entry overhead for both kernels across seqlen buckets and add it to the perf suite.

alana: Thanks all — keeping this thread for postmortem notes. If anyone finds flaky CI diffs for memory, ping here. :thumbsup:
